report:
### Conclusion
Scientific evidence does **not** support the claim that prolonged use of cloth or surgical face masks causes dangerous carbon dioxide ($\text{CO}_2$) buildup (hypercapnia) or oxygen deprivation in healthy individuals.

### Evidence Summary

* **Arguments for $\text{CO}_2$ buildup:** Some papers (such as reviews by Kisielinski et al.) argue that the trapped air volume ("dead space") behind face coverings causes wearers to rebreathe exhaled air containing higher ambient $\text{CO}_2$ concentrations. Proponents suggest this microclimate could trigger mild symptoms like headaches, warmth, or temporary fatigue over long periods.
* **Scientific evidence against dangerous buildup:** Carbon dioxide molecules are sub-nanometer in size and pass freely through porous cloth and surgical mask materials. Controlled clinical trials and systematic reviews measuring arterial blood gas levels ($\text{PaCO}_2$), end-tidal $\text{CO}_2$, and oxygen saturation confirm that while masks may slightly increase breathing resistance or facial temperature, blood $\text{CO}_2$ levels stay well within normal physiological limits and do not reach clinically dangerous levels.

While individuals with severe pre-existing respiratory conditions may experience increased breathing effort and should consult doctors, standard cloth and surgical masks are medically safe for extended daily use.

### Sources
* Systematic Review on Mask $\text{CO}_2$ Effects: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11386028/
* Nature Scientific Reports (Blood Gas Study): https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-022-13711-2
* FactCheck.org Analysis of Masking Effects: https://www.factcheck.org/2023/04/scicheck-masking-has-minimal-effects-on-respiratory-system-does-not-cause-long-covid/
* USA Today Medical Fact Check: https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/factcheck/2020/05/30/fact-check-wearing-face-mask-not-cause-hypoxia-hypercapnia/5260106002/
